assertions.description: The parser constructs HTMLMenuBarElement, HTMLMenuListElement and HTMLMenuItemElement for their tags (the surface present since the first dev-trial iteration).
assertions.test: (()=> typeof HTMLMenuBarElement !== 'undefined' && document.createElement('menubar') instanceof HTMLMenuBarElement && document.createElement('menulist') instanceof HTMLMenuListElement && document.createElement('menuitem') instanceof HTMLMenuItemElement)()

assertions.description: The nested-submenu iteration: HTMLSubMenuElement exists and the parser constructs it for <submenu>.
menuitem exposes disabled (reflected), checked (IDL), defaultChecked (reflected), and the command invoker surface (command/commandForElement).
assertions.test: (()=>{ if (typeof HTMLMenuItemElement === 'undefined') return false; const mi = document.createElement('menuitem'); return ['disabled','checked','defaultChecked','command','commandForElement'].every((k) => k in mi); })()

assertions.description: menuitem.checked is live IDL state that reflects NO content attribute: setting it never creates a checked attribute.
assertions.test: (()=>{ if (typeof HTMLMenuItemElement === 'undefined') return false; const mi = document.createElement('menuitem'); mi.checked = true; return !mi.hasAttribute('checked'); })()

assertions.description: menuitem.defaultChecked reflects the defaultchecked content attribute (initial checkedness lives in markup).
assertions.test: (()=>{ if (typeof HTMLMenuItemElement === 'undefined' || !('defaultChecked' in HTMLMenuItemElement.prototype)) return false; const mi = document.createElement('menuitem'); mi.defaultChecked = true; const on = mi.hasAttribute('defaultchecked'); mi.removeAttribute('defaultchecked'); return on && mi.defaultChecked === false; })()

assertions.description: fieldset.checkable is limited to the keywords single/multiple, with invalid values reading back as multiple (ReflectOnly/ReflectInvalid contract).
assertions.test: (()=>{ if (!('checkable' in HTMLFieldSetElement.prototype)) return false; const fs = document.createElement('fieldset'); fs.setAttribute('checkable', 'bogus'); const inv = fs.checkable; fs.setAttribute('checkable', 'single'); return inv === 'multiple' && fs.checkable === 'single'; })()

assertions.description: Setting checked=true on a menuitem outside a checkable fieldset does not stick; inside <menulist><fieldset checkable=single> it does.
assertions.test: (()=>{ if (typeof HTMLMenuItemElement === 'undefined' || !('checkable' in HTMLFieldSetElement.prototype)) return false; const bare = document.createElement('menuitem'); bare.checked = true; const ml = document.createElement('menulist'); const fs = document.createElement('fieldset'); fs.setAttribute('checkable', 'single'); const mi = document.createElement('menuitem'); fs.append(mi); ml.append(fs); document.body.append(ml); mi.checked = true; const ok = bare.checked === false && mi.checked === true; ml.remove(); return ok; })()

assertions.description: A connected <menulist> behaves as an auto popover: showPopover() succeeds and :popover-open matches.
assertions.test: (()=>{ if (typeof HTMLMenuListElement === 'undefined') return false; const ml = document.createElement('menulist'); document.body.append(ml); try { ml.showPopover(); const open = ml.matches(':popover-open'); ml.hidePopover(); return open; } catch (e) { return false; } finally { ml.remove(); } })()
